statement: For the parameters above, Stolarski’s construction supplies a smooth Ricci flow up to a finite time T on Sp × Sq+1 with the following properties, after translating its starting time to zero. (i) Off the two pole orbits it has the form g = ds2 + ϕ2 gSp + r2 gSq . Here s is radial arclength at each time. The metric is invariant under reflection exchanging the poles. On each open hemisphere, oriented from its pole toward the equator, rs > 0. At a pole, r = 0, rs = 1, and ϕs = 0; the usual odd and even polar expansions hold for r and ϕ, respectively, and ϕ > 0 for every t < T. 3 (ii) Write u = log ϕ, z = r2 s , and e U = log ϕ (A/B)r , e Z = z − B2 . There are positive tolerances ηU j , ηZ j , large fixed numbers 1 < Y1 ≤ Y2, and constants M0 > 0, 0 < β < 1/2, such that for j = 0, 1, 2, ∂ j γ( e U − δν Uk) ≤ ηU j δν γ−d−j + γ2k−d  , ∂ j γ(e Z − δν Zk) ≤ ηZ j δν γ−d−j + γ2k−d  . (2.3) The first estimate holds from Y1δν/d to M0eβτ, and the second from Y2δν/d to that upper endpoint, within the hemisphere. The profiles are smooth on γ > 0. The function Uk is γ−d times a polynomial of degree k in γ2, with positive leading coefficients at zero and infinity: Uk(γ) ∼ c1γ−d (γ ↓ 0), Uk(γ) ∼ c2γ2k−d (γ → ∞), c1, c2 > 0. Also Zk(γ) = Oq,k(γ−d) as γ ↓ 0. (iii) For all sufficiently late times, putting f = rur, one has ϕ/r ≥ A/B, 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, fr ≥ 0 (0 < r ≤ Y1θ), B2 ≤ z ≤ 1 (0 < r ≤ Y2θ). (2.4) These inner intervals lie strictly below the equator. (iv) At the initial time τ0 = − log T, the same weighted profile bounds hold up to an initial outer cutoff Ginit = M0eβinitτ0 , where 0 < βinit < 1/2, and e U ≥ 0 beyond that cutoff. The exponents are chosen in the ranges permitted by the construction; in particular, one may take 0 < β < ν 2ν + 1 ≤ βinit < 1 2 . They are therefore distinct choices, not two arbitrary exponents. The tolerances can be chosen sufficiently small depending on q, k. The inner cutoffs can then be increased in order, first Y1 and then Y2; the initial rescaled time can subsequently be increased. Each such increase is subject only to lower-size requirements from the construction.
